title: Twofold universality of large-$N$ melonic random tensors
abstract: We construct a measure that exhibits two aspects of a new type of universality and dramatically simplifies the integration of tensors $T_{a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_D} \in \mathbb{C}$ ($a_1,\ldots,a_D=1,\ldots,N$) at large $N$. In contrast to matrix integration, in which matrix traces canonically yield the integrand, tensors need additional information (equivalent to a $D$-coloured graph $B$) to contract their indices and form a tensor trace $B(T)$. We show that, whenever each $B_1,\ldots, B_n$ can be obtained by a recursive construction known as melonicity, then the leading order in $N$ of the integral of $ {B_1}(T) {B_2}(T) \cdots {B_n}(T) $ is independent of the -- often intricate -- combinatorics of the traces $B_i$, but also, to our surprise, independent of $D$ as far as $D\geq 3$. Instead, at large $N$, these integrals are some functions (indexed by $n$) of the number of vertices $2p_i$ of $B_i$ which we call melonic polynomials. Melonic traces cumulants with respect to any ('interacting') measure \[ \exp\Big\{-N^{D-1} \sum_{i=1}^m g_i {B_i}(T)\Big\} \mathrm{d}μ_0(T) \quad (g_1,\ldots,g_m \in \mathbb{R}, \mathrm{d}μ_0(T) =\text{the tensor Gaussian}) \] with each $B_i$ melonic, can be computed with our universal measure that replaces each $B_i$ by a canonical trace depending only on $p_i$. We prove that any two melonic tensor models are indistinguishable at large-$N$, independently of the number of tensor indices (first universality aspect), and of the fine-grainedness of their interactions (second universality), being a sufficient condition that the couplings (the parameters $g_i$ above) agree and their respective traces are monomials with the same degree in $T$.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a powerful 'twofold universality' result for integrals involving large-$N$ melonic random tensors. It shows that these complex tensor integrals simplify significantly at large $N$, depending only on simple polynomial functions of the graph structure, regardless of the specific details of the interaction or dimension. This provides a universal framework for calculating correlation functions in high-dimensional statistical models.
main_problem: The authors investigate constructing a measure exhibiting 'twofold universality' for integrating large-$N$ random tensors, which are generalizations of matrix integrals.
main_result: They prove that these tensor integrals simplify dramatically at large $N$, becoming independent of intricate combinatorics and the dimensionality $D$ (for $D\geq 3$), depending only on 'melonic polynomials'.
method: The analysis involves computing connected correlation functions using Wick contractions ($\pi$) over graph structures, establishing uniqueness theorems for maximal contractions, and comparing cumulants across different theoretical models.
model_or_system: The model is based on random tensors $T_{a_1,\ldots,a_D}$ integrated with respect to a Gaussian measure. The complexity arises from the need to contract indices using graph structures called 'melonic graphs' ($B$), which are analogues of matrix traces.
key_observables: Melonic polynomials (functions indexed by $n$ related to vertex counts), and the large-$N$ limit of tensor cumulants $\langle B_1 \dots B_n angle$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the tensors are 'melonic' (satisfying a recursive construction) and relies on proving convergence of ratios of cumulants to establish universality.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate graph structures, such as gluings of $2p$-agons analogous to matrix integrals, and show diagrams related to critical loci and two-point functions for the quartic tensor model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem (tensor integration), establishing tools like maximal Wick contractions ($\pi_{	ext{max}}$) via graph theory, proving universality theorems (Theorem 4.2 and 5.1), and finally applying these results to confirm the 'twofold universality' of the large-$N$ limit.
why_interesting: The concept of universal behavior emerging from complex combinatorial structures (tensors/graphs) at large $N$ is highly relevant in statistical mechanics, particularly when studying critical phenomena or random matrix theories generalized to higher dimensions.
